The likely fix is in `printUrl` in `src/language-markdown/print/mdast.js`. I read the code but didn't run Prettier on the report's input.

The parser turns `&quot\;bar` into the URL `foo"bar`. It decodes the `\;` escape, so the printer no longer sees a backslash. The printer then has to put the backslash back, because `"` would read as a character reference on the next pass.

`printUrl` (line 464) already calls `escapeCharacterReferences`, which rewrites `&name;` to `\&name;`. That helper is a one-line arrow function at line 456, and its regex is `characterReferenceRegex` at line 454. A bug here would most likely be in how that regex matches.

The `"link"` case at line 168 calls `printUrl(node.url, false)` at line 190. The case would only need to change if the fix has to look at the original source text.

The current code seems to already handle this input, so the fix may be partly in place. Check this checkout against the reported v3.9.5 output before changing anything.

The fix belongs in the CLI's error handling in `src/cli/format.js`. I read the code but didn't run the CLI or reproduce the bug.

- **`handleError`** decides what happens when a file has no inferable parser. It logs the error and sets `process.exitCode = 2` (`src/cli/format.js:44-47`). It returns `true` instead when `ignoreUnknown` is set, which skips the error and the exit code. That `ignoreUnknown` flag comes from the CLI option or from `expand-patterns.js:101`.
- **`formatFiles`** counts files with errors from `handleError`'s return value (`src/cli/format.js:384-394`). It then prints the `--check` summary: "Error occurred…" or "All matched files use Prettier code style!" (`src/cli/format.js:472-494`). It also contains the final `--check` exit-code logic (`src/cli/format.js:497-503`).

In the report the error is logged, yet the summary says "All matched files use Prettier code style!" and the exit code is 0. That means the error count stayed at 0 and the exit code was never set. The current code looks like it should set exit code 2 here, so the regression may sit in how `ignoreUnknown` is passed in or how `handleError`'s return value is used. I didn't confirm which. `expandPatterns` (`src/cli/expand-patterns.js:18`) is a less likely third place to look.

The function to change is `printTypeParameters` in `src/language-js/print/type-parameters.js`. I read the code but did not run Prettier on the report's input, so this is from reading, not from a reproduction.

The "inline" path starts at line 84 (`shouldInline`) and prints `<`, the parameters, then `>` with no indent or line breaks. It is only skipped when the single parameter has a leading or trailing line comment, and that check only looks at comments attached directly to `parameters[0]`. For `foo<// Comment\nType>`, the comment is probably attached to a child node, such as the `typeName` identifier inside the `TSTypeReference`. If so, the check misses it, the inline path is used, and the output is `foo<// Comment\nType>`. The fix is to make that check also catch comments on the inner node. That would send the case to the grouped path at line 121, which indents with `softline`.

The trailing-comma handling for `var()` lives in `src/language-css/print/parenthesized-value-group.js`, so that's where the fix belongs. I read the code but didn't run Prettier on the report's input to reproduce the output.

- **`printTrailingComma` (line 51):** This is the only place a trailing comma is emitted inside a `var()` call. It does so only when `hasTrailingComma` returns true.
- **`hasTrailingComma` (line 32):** This looks at the character after the last value to find a `,`. It would have to be the function that fails for `var(--baz,)`. I didn't confirm why. It looks for the last non-comment child and returns false if there isn't one. It also checks `parent.type` against `"value-paren_group"`. Either check may not match how the parser represents a bare comma with an empty fallback.
- **`printParenthesizedValueGroup` (line 78):** This calls `printTrailingComma` only for the last group (`isLast`, line 131). If the parser drops the empty group after the comma, the comma would have to be re-added here.
- **`isVarFunctionNode` (`src/language-css/utilities/index.js:124`):** This decides whether the grandparent is a `var()` call. I'm less sure it needs to change.
